speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long this painful ulcerative lesion on your leg has been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size or appearance? Also, do you have any history of diabetes, vascular disease, or recent injuries to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion's progression after an insect bite, could you describe the borders of the ulcer—are they raised and violaceous with undermined edges? Also, have you experienced any systemic symptoms like fever, joint pain, or new eye inflammation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a painful ulcer with a necrotic base, violaceous undermined borders, and a history of Crohn's disease strongly suggests pyoderma gangrenosum, particularly given the pathergy triggered by the ant bite. I will now confirm this clinical suspicion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
